Head of Engineering
Stealth Startup
Boston, MA
$170,000.00/yr - $210,000.00/yr
Head of Engineering – AI & Healthcare Technology
What You'll Own
AI Systems and Engineering Leverage
Own how the company uses AI models, including model selection, deployment, and cost optimization. Continuously improve the product as models evolve, using less expensive models where they meet the required quality standards.
Build evaluation frameworks and quality feedback loops to demonstrate, with evidence, whether documentation is accurate, complete, and consistent, and whether new capabilities are ready for real-world clinical practices.
Empower engineers and non-engineers to build and ship products using the best available AI models and development tools. Continuously improve team workflows as these tools advance, while maintaining high standards for the quality and security of customer-facing releases.
Systems and Delivery
Own end-to-end R&D delivery, translating ambiguous customer needs into reliable, production-ready software for a growing multi-tenant healthcare platform.
Standardize phone system integrations to make onboarding new medical practices faster, more efficient, and repeatable.
Maintain exceptionally high standards for correctness and data integrity across integrations with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), telephony systems, and third-party APIs.
Understand and optimize the complete cost of product delivery, including telephony, transcription, and AI model usage, while designing for sustainable unit economics.
Reliability and Security
Improve system reliability through robust observability, alerting, incident response processes, and deployment pipelines.
Build security and compliance into the platform by default, including HIPAA compliance, encryption, and auditability, and establish standards for the engineering team to follow.
Technical Leadership
Define the team's technical direction and build alignment around architectural decisions and engineering priorities.
Hire exceptional engineers who raise the bar and foster a culture that combines AI-driven ambition with rigorous quality standards.
Improve engineering capabilities through code reviews, design discussions, and collaborative programming.
Partner with clinical and product stakeholders to translate requirements into sound, scalable technical solutions.
Customer Empathy and Product Excellence
Understand how nurses, healthcare providers, and practice staff rely on the platform in their daily workflows. Identify gaps, prioritize improvements, and ensure solutions are delivered effectively.
Pay close attention to user experience details, including presenting information more clearly, reducing unnecessary clicks, and making the next action intuitive.
Represent the customer's perspective within the engineering organization, ensuring the team remains focused on the people and workflows the product serves.
What Good Looks Like
You bring energy and urgency to the work, helping the team tackle meaningful and challenging problems every day.
Each new generation of AI models improves the product, and adopting new models becomes a routine process rather than requiring a major rebuild.
Product documentation quality is measured with evidence, and new capabilities reach customers only after meeting established quality standards.
A small engineering team delivers an exceptional amount of work because AI is embedded throughout its development processes.
New medical practices are onboarded through standardized, repeatable integrations, allowing the platform to scale across more practices and enterprise customers without compromising reliability or security.
The cost of delivering the product decreases as usage grows.
Engineers continuously improve through your feedback, standards, and established engineering practices, while new hires further strengthen the team.
The CEO and the wider team trust you to make critical technical decisions, allowing others to focus on their respective priorities.
What We're Looking For
Must Have
7+ years of experience building and owning production systems, including experience hiring and leading engineering teams.
Hands-on experience building with Large Language Models (LLMs), not just building infrastructure around them. You have shipped LLM-powered features to production and managed post-launch challenges such as evaluation, quality drift, latency, and cost.
Strong awareness of the latest AI developments. You actively experiment with new models and agentic tools, have a clear perspective on their future direction, and can distinguish genuine technological breakthroughs from hype.
AI-first engineering practices. You use AI coding tools and agents daily and have transformed how a team works through improved workflows, tooling, code reviews, and task ownership.
Experience making architectural decisions that hold up under real-world conditions and designing systems that improve as AI models evolve, without requiring a complete rebuild with every release.
Exceptional software engineering fundamentals and experience designing large-scale systems, combined with a strong understanding of how AI changes team responsibilities and software development practices.
Ability to work autonomously in fast-moving, ambiguous environments while bringing clarity, alignment, and momentum to the wider team.
Experience joining an existing team and codebase, earning credibility with established engineers, and raising standards through influence, practical contributions, and effective processes.
Strong Signals
Experience in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated industries, with familiarity with compliance requirements such as HIPAA, encryption, and auditability.
Experience with real-time voice systems, including telephony, streaming audio, speech-to-text, or WebSockets.
Experience building integrations with EHRs or other complex third-party systems and making those integrations standardized and repeatable.
Who This Role Is Not For
You prefer managing from a distance and leaving architecture, development processes, and the quality of customer-facing releases to others.
You measure success by the number of people reporting to you.
You expect a fully researched Product Requirements Document (PRD) for every change rather than taking ownership of a problem and driving it forward.
You view AI as just another roadmap feature or prefer waiting for tools and best practices to stabilize before adopting them.
You are excited about the newest AI models but not about the work required to make them reliable for clinicians during live calls.
You want to focus exclusively on technical challenges while leaving customer problems and pain points to others.
Compensation
Base Salary:
Competitive compensation for a seed-stage healthcare technology company.
Equity:
Early-stage equity grant, offering the opportunity to join early and help build the engineering organization from the ground up.

Vice President, Enterprise Quality & Automation
SS&C Technologies
Atlanta, GA
SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely. Founded in 1986, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has offices worldwide. More than 23,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology.
Job Description
Vice President, Enterprise Quality & Automation
Locations: Atlanta, GA, Jacksonville, FL, Fort Worth, TX
About The Role
As Vice President of Enterprise Quality & Automation, you will own the quality our clients and operations actually experience across pharmacy and medical — from requirements and vendor execution through UAT, release readiness, defect management, automation, and AI enablement.
Quality isn't produced by any single team. It takes shape across the entire delivery process. This leader works across Product, Technology, Operations, and vendors to set quality standards, surface risk early, and align everyone toward shared outcomes. The VP will also help define how far this capability should go, from strengthening quality today, to establishing a durable operating model, to evolving quality, automation, and testing into scalable commercial offerings over time. The path is not fully defined by design: we want a leader who is energized by ambiguity and eager to shape the strategy and roadmap rather than inherit them. This role reports into the SVP, Operations, and will build and lead a team of four to six direct reports at the Director level. The leader will help shape how that team is structured and grows over time.
Why Join SS&C
SS&C combines proprietary technology with deep industry expertise to support complex financial and health care operations. Our teams design, implement, and operate solutions that help clients manage data, automate processes, and scale their businesses with confidence.
You will work with industry experts, modern platforms, and evolving technologies, gaining exposure to real-world operational challenges and large-scale enterprise environments.
What Makes This Role Different
A mandate to shape the function. You will build and lead a team of four to six and shape its structure and operating model as the strategy takes shape. A rare chance to design a capability rather than inherit one.
Real influence across the enterprise. You are the trusted voice on quality across Product, Technology, Operations, and vendors; setting standards, surfacing risk, and driving decisions at the executive level, with the visibility and mandate to make quality a priority.
AI and automation are central. These are major parts of the strategy, from predictive quality analytics and defect prediction to release-risk assessment and intelligent automation.
Commercial upside. You will evaluate how these capabilities can evolve into scalable, revenue-generating offerings.
How You Will Make An Impact
Strategy & Operating Model
Define the enterprise quality strategy and target operating model across pharmacy and medical.
Establish quality standards, governance, and release-readiness criteria across the lifecycle, in partnership with delivery teams.
Recommend and sequence the operating model with a transition roadmap, metrics, and governance.
Partnership & Governance
Partner with Product, Technology, Operations, and vendors to align on quality expectations and shared accountability.
Provide independent assessments of quality, readiness, and risk to inform executive and delivery decisions.
Strengthen how requirements, UAT, and release readiness work together across organizations.
AI & Automation
Set the AI and automation strategy for quality: predictive analytics, defect prediction, release-risk assessment, and intelligent automation.
Build the business case for investment and quantify impact on quality, speed, and cost.
Establish responsible, auditable AI practices appropriate to a regulated healthcare environment.
Defect Management & Continuous Improvement
Lead enterprise defect management, root-cause analysis, and defect-leakage reduction.
Define quality metrics that measure outcomes and inform decisions.
Build a continuous-improvement engine that raises quality and lowers cost over time.
Vendor Quality & Scalable Delivery
Set quality expectations and accountability for vendor execution, and manage vendor and offshore delivery models toward scalable, multi-customer delivery.
Assess and, if warranted, build quality and testing capabilities into a commercial service offering.
Leadership
Build and lead a high-performing enterprise quality function with clear accountability and metrics.
Communicate credibly at the executive level, translating quality into business impact.
Bring clarity to open-ended problems and lead cross-organizational change.
Scope & Boundaries
This leader owns enterprise quality strategy, standards, and outcomes, and partners closely with the teams who own delivery. The role is designed to work through influence and shared accountability, and how the team is built out will take shape with the leader who steps into it.
Leads: enterprise quality strategy, standards, and governance; quality metrics, defect and root-cause management, and release-readiness criteria; the automation and AI strategy for quality; and an independent view of quality, readiness, and risk.
Partners on: requirements (Product), solution design (Technology), UAT and operational readiness (Operations), and vendor execution; setting quality expectations and driving alignment, while these teams own their own delivery.
The Team You'll Build (Illustrative Starting Point)
This is a starting structure, not a fixed design. The incoming VP will shape how it evolves.
Director, Test Operations: SIT, regression, release testing, defect management, test planning
Director, UAT & Business Validation: Cognizant and customer UAT, business UAT, end-to-end testing readiness
Director, Quality Engineering & Automation: automation, AI-enabled testing, performance testing, frameworks, tooling
Director, Testing Services & Vendor Strategy: vendor management, RFP support, capacity planning, Testing-as-a-Service commercialization
Required Experience
Significant leadership experience in enterprise quality or quality assurance, across in-house and vendor/partner-based delivery.
Demonstrated experience defining and standing up a quality operating model, governance, or transformation at scale across multiple organizations.
Track record of driving quality outcomes through partnership and governance rather than direct ownership of delivery teams.
Strong command of quality metrics, defect management, root-cause analysis, UAT, and release readiness.
Practical experience applying AI/ML and automation to quality, with a clear point of view on where they create value.
Experience managing vendor and offshore delivery models and holding partners accountable to quality standards.
Comfort operating amid ambiguity — defining strategy and structure where none yet exists and leading change.
Executive-level communication that translates quality into business impact.
Healthcare experience, particularly pharmacy claims and PBM; medical claims and health plan experience.
What Sets You Apart
Experience commercializing an internal capability into an external service offering.
Background with large-scale platform migrations and complex, multi-system integration.
P&L or commercial ownership experience.
The Leader We're Looking For
You are a builder and a strategist who thrives when the destination isn't fully mapped. You think in terms of the quality clients and operations actually experience, and you know that depends on many teams working well together — so you lead through partnership and influence rather than control. You are a trusted, independent voice across Product, Technology, Operations, and vendors, and you lead with evidence, metrics, and economics. You see AI and automation as major levers for how quality gets done, and you're motivated by the rare chance to shape a capability that could grow into a commercial business.
Join SS&C, where innovation meets global opportunities. Click here to apply.
Unless explicitly requested or approached by SS&C Technologies, Inc. or any of its affiliated companies, the company will not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.
SS&C Technologies offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and future. Our benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) plan with company match; paid time off, holidays, and parental leave; and professional development reimbursement opportunity.

Senior Manager, Product Operations
Anduril Industries
Costa Mesa, California, United States
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Frontier Systems (AFS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized hardware and software products for defense, law enforcement, and intelligence customers. We work alongside our customers to understand their requirements and deliver exquisite capabilities across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements.
Product Operations is the team accountable for the health of the systems and technology that delivers the capabilities that our customers depend on. The function identifies, triages, and drives resolution of incidents across the deployed fleet, and converts what we've learned into the reliability and sustainment insights that product and engineering teams act upon. We work in close coordination with product engineering, reliability, quality, program management, and field operations teams to maximize capability availability for our end users and inform the next cycle of iterations.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As the Senior Manager of Product Operations for Frontier Systems, you will own product operations across the division's product portfolio and the programs that deliver those products. You will lead multiple Product Operations managers, each of whom runs a team of technical specialists and engineers focused on supporting and improving fielded products. The division's portfolio is scaling, and this role exists to scale support alongside it, both for the products the function covers today and for the ones that reach the field next.
This is a function maturation and growth role as much as an operating one, and the work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic systems, and the judgment to make decisions whose impact reaches beyond your own team and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Lead and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Frontier Systems portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also maturing the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people in it.
Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and to internal Anduril teams. Understand the work at every level, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.
Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.
Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning for the function and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.
Own the Failure Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop: Own the workflow that converts field failures into structured, trustworthy signal for product and reliability engineering, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Partner with engineering to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your own organization accountable to its fidelity.
Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Mature the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.
Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes.
Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.
Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.
Travel and Availability: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations, and to work non-standard hours when fielded operations require it.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains).
Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support).
Organizational Leadership: Experience leading managers and multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program.
Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.
Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.
Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.
Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.
Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning for a function and stating the assumptions behind the model.
Program Management: Project and program management ability applied outside a project management role: decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions.
Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.
Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.
Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:
Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.
Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading air defense, intelligence, and/or force protection teams.
Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management disciplines (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).
Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.
Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.
Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded robotic and sensor systems, including actuation, power systems, sensing, embedded compute, radar, RF detection, and electro-optical and infrared sensing, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.
Comfort reading logs, telemetry, and test data, including hands-on use of Linux command-line interfaces and tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, Git, SQL, and Palantir Foundry.
Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.
Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.
Experience in on-call support operations and limited risk tolerance environments.
An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.

Job Description
DescriptionDirector of Operations - Wisconsin & Illinois
Department: Operations
Reports To: COO
Location: Wisconsin and Illinois; regular travel between assigned facilities
Direct Reports: Assigned General Managers, and Site Managers
Summary
The Director of Operations leads the operational and financial performance of the company's Wisconsin and Illinois facilities. This position oversees conventional caged and cage-free layer production, pullet operations where assigned, shell egg grading and packing, egg breaking and liquid egg processing, feed mills, and supporting operational functions.
The Director translates company strategy into clear site-level priorities, develops strong leaders, and holds teams accountable for safe operations, animal welfare, food safety, customer service, and profitability. This role requires a visible, hands-on leader who drives consistent execution, improves operating practices, and builds collaboration across locations and corporate functions.
Key Responsibilities
Regional Leadership and Accountability
Lead regional operations to achieve production, processing, quality, service, and financial goals.
Establish clear expectations, performance measures, and operating plans for each facility.
Hold General Managers and operational leaders accountable for results, timely corrective actions, and follow-through.
Maintain a regular presence at facilities to evaluate conditions, coach leaders, and address operational barriers.
Standardize effective practices across locations while accounting for differences in housing systems, equipment, and customer requirements.
Communicate performance, risks, resource needs, and recommendations to executive leadership.
Live Production and Animal Welfare
Oversee conventional caged and cage-free layer operations.
Oversee pullet rearing and replacement flock readiness where assigned.
Drive flock performance through effective management of production, mortality, livability, egg quality, feed conversion, body weight, and flock uniformity.
Ensure consistent execution of ventilation, lighting, water, feeding, litter, and manure management programs.
Partner with veterinary and nutrition teams on flock health, disease prevention, vaccination, pest control, and nutrition programs.
Ensure compliance with company animal welfare standards and applicable certification and customer requirements.
Enforce biosecurity expectations for employees, visitors, equipment, contractors, and transportation.
Shell Egg and Breaking Operations
Oversee shell egg receiving, grading, packing, storage, and shipping.
Oversee egg breaking and liquid egg processing, including pasteurization where applicable.
Improve egg recovery, saleable yield, throughput, labor efficiency, equipment utilization, and product quality.
Reduce checks, cracks, losses, rework, downtime, and customer complaints.
Coordinate production and processing schedules with sales, planning, and logistics to meet customer commitments and manage inventory.
Partner with Quality Assurance to maintain sanitation, traceability, food safety programs, audit readiness, and timely corrective actions.
Ensure reported production, gradeout, yield, and inventory results are accurate and supported by operational records.
Feed Mill Operations
Oversee assigned feed mills to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective feed manufacturing and delivery.
Align mill capacity, production schedules, and delivery plans with flock requirements.
Partner with nutrition and procurement teams on ingredient quality, availability, formulation implementation, and inventory management.
Ensure controls for batching accuracy, mixing consistency, ingredient receiving, storage, sanitation, and feed traceability.
Monitor feed manufacturing costs, shrink, downtime, maintenance needs, and delivery performance.
Address feed quality concerns promptly with appropriate technical and operational support.
Financial and Business Performance
Own regional operating performance against approved budgets and business plans.
Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, labor planning, and capital planning for assigned operations.
Review site financial results and operating metrics to identify variances, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.
Improve cost per dozen, processing costs, feed manufacturing costs, asset utilization, and overall profitability.
Ensure purchasing discipline, accurate inventory controls, and compliance with spending authority.
Develop capital requests supported by operational need, expected benefits, financial justification, and implementation plans.
Maintenance and Supporting Operations
Oversee maintenance, preventive maintenance, equipment reliability, utilities, and facility condition.
Support transportation, egg movements, feed delivery, warehousing, and other assigned logistics activities.
Ensure effective manure handling, storage, and removal, along with environmental stewardship and housekeeping.
Coordinate contractors, construction, equipment installations, and facility improvement projects.
Maintain emergency response and business continuity plans for disease events, fires, utility failures, severe weather, and equipment breakdowns.
People, Safety, and Culture
Build and develop a capable regional leadership team through coaching, succession planning, and performance management.
Partner with Human Resources on staffing, retention, training, employee relations, and leadership development.
Set clear expectations for professional communication, teamwork, and respectful treatment of employees.
Promote a culture in which employees raise concerns, leaders address issues promptly, and commitments are completed.
Partner with EHS and site leadership to improve workplace safety, investigate incidents, and close corrective actions.
Ensure employees receive appropriate training and have the resources needed to perform their work safely and effectively.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in poultry science, agriculture, operations management, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered.
Typically 10 or more years of progressive agricultural or food manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility across multiple facilities.
Strong knowledge of commercial layer production, including conventional caged and cage-free systems.
Experience overseeing shell egg processing, egg breaking, and feed mill operations strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, interpret financial results, and improve operational performance.
Working knowledge of animal welfare, biosecurity, food safety, employee safety, and environmental requirements.
Proven ability to develop leaders, manage change, resolve problems, and hold teams accountable.
Strong communication, planning, analytical, and decision-making skills.
Measures of Success
Performance will be evaluated through a balanced set of regional and site-level measures, including:
Financial: Budget performance, controllable costs, and verified improvement results.
Live production: Egg production, mortality, livability, feed conversion, and egg quality.
Processing: Yield, recovery, throughput, labor efficiency, downtime, and order fulfillment.
Feed mills: Feed quality, manufacturing cost, inventory accuracy, and delivery reliability.
People and safety: Leadership development, retention, training completion, safety performance, and corrective action closure.
Compliance and execution: Animal welfare and food safety results, data accuracy, audit readiness, and completion of operating and capital priorities.
Working Conditions
This position requires frequent travel between Wisconsin and Illinois facilities and availability to support operations outside normal business hours when necessary. Work includes time in poultry houses, processing plants, feed mills, and outdoor environments, with required adherence to site biosecurity, food safety, and personal protective equipment procedures.

Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, OEE improvement, 5S, visual management, waste reduction, changeover optimization, downtime reduction, and continuous improvement.

Create an environment conducive to the development of teammates primarily through timely coaching, feedback, and recognition, helping ensure everyone has an opportunity to do their best work.
Manage staffing, labor planning, productivity, and budget performance while ensuring the organization is appropriately resourced to meet daily execution and long-term business needs.
